questions.question: S1: A synthetic client reads task-owned fixture updates from a scratch server and displays a simple status indicator. Which isolated validation path should this harmless probe use?

L2: The synthetic probe records harmless fixture markers while its scratch client displays a status indicator. Which isolated timing choice should this validation keep without changing a user preference?

options.label: Keep the synthetic timing (Recommended)
options.description: Observe only the synthetic marker and retain the task-owned capture so the exact native answer can be checked against the structured hook result.

options.label: Record the next marker
options.description: Observe the subsequent harmless marker in the same isolated fixture without changing any persistent preference or touching another runtime.

questions.question: L3: Several synthetic fixture checks share this task-owned scratch transcript: a local status marker, a harmless text update, and a captured review page. Which final summary should the isolated validation retain while preserving all existing user settings?

options.label: Keep synthetic result evidence
options.description: Preserve the public synthetic capture and exact structured answers for the current-source validation report, then stop only this task-owned runtime.

options.label: Keep a short summary
options.description: Keep only a brief task-owned summary of the fixture result, with no account, credential, policy, server, or user-session changes.
